2. Sri Renspre Prithesh D'souza, learned counsel appearing for petitioner submitted that land bearing Sy.no.77/1A1A17 of Subramanya Village, Kadaba Taluk, D.K. District, measuring 03 cents was acquired by respondent no.3 for purposes of road as per Master Plan.
In said regard, an award was passed on 08.08.2016 fixing compensation at `1,16,323/-.
It was submitted that notice was issued to petitioner under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, on 08.08.2016.

In response to same, petitioner filed application on 19.08.2016, wherein he had stated that there were structures etc., which were not assessed for compensation and therefore, sought for correction of award.

3. It was submitted that in pursuance of petitioner's application, communication at Annexure-R was made by Deputy Commissioner, Mangaluru to respondent no.1 dated NC: 2023:KHC:40435 31.03.2022 and in it's reply by respondent no.1 dated 24.05.2022 as per Annexure-A, it is stated that there cannot be correction of award since application was filed after 51/2 years.
Assailing same, this writ petition is filed.
4. It was submitted that since application was filed within time and respondents were required to consider same in accordance with law.
Without considering same, impugned order was passed and therefore sought for allowing writ petition.

5. On other hand, Sri Yogesh D. Naik, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for respondents would submit that both Annexure-R as well as Annexure-A were internal correspondences between Government and Deputy Commissioner and therefore could not be challenged by petitioner, and since same had fortified into an order, writ petition would not be tenable.

sentences.text: In reply, learned counsel for petitioner would submit that upon receipt of award notice under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, petitioner had submitted application on 19.08.2016.

Same was referred to by Special Land Acquisition Officer in its communication to Executive Engineer dated NC: 2023:KHC:40435 25.08.2016 at Annexure-K. It was submitted that since said application was filed by petitioner immediately upon receipt of notice under Section 12(2) of Land Acquisition Act, there was no justification for observing that application was filed after 51/2 years.
7.

Further, Section 33 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'LA Act, 2013') would provide for making correction to award by Collector if mistakes are pointed out within six months.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Since within two weeks of passing of award, petitioner had pointed out that structures in acquired land had not been valued, same ought to have been considered by respondents.
And though, Annexures-R and A were internal correspondences, petitioner's application for correction would require to be considered.

8. Consequently, writ petition is disposed of by directing respondents no.2 and 3 to consider petitioner's application/representation dated 19.08.2016, as application for correction in terms of Section 33 of LA Act, 2013, and pass appropriate orders thereon within period of three months and result of such consideration be communicated to petitioner.
In case, application is already considered, respondents to communicate decision thereon to petitioner.
Liberty is reserved to petitioner to agitate his right, if aggrieved thereby.

Needles to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.
